title: Same Payload, Different Channel: Measuring Trust Asymmetry in Tool-Using Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2606.00566v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As language models take on agentic roles that call APIs, read tool outputs, and act on third-party content, their attack surface expands beyond what users type. Whether they treat a malicious instruction the same way regardless of where it arrives has not been studied systematically. We introduce the Safety Asymmetry Score (SAS), measuring how a model's susceptibility to adversarial content shifts depending on whether it arrives in the user message, tool metadata, or tool output, using matched payload pairs that hold the malicious text identical and vary only the channel. Across 10 production LLMs and three attack families, general-purpose models sharply discount instructions arriving as tool metadata relative to identical instructions in the user message, while agent-native models discount them far less. This differential survives an affordance-matched control equalizing tool availability and scoring, and a size-controlled mix

translated_title: 相同载荷，不同渠道：衡量工具使用型语言模型中的信任不对称性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2606.00566v2 公告类型：替换交叉 摘要：随着语言模型承担起调用API、读取工具输出并对第三方内容采取行动的代理角色，其攻击面已扩展到用户输入之外。无论恶意指令来自何处，模型是否以相同方式处理，尚未得到系统研究。我们引入了安全不对称分数（SAS），通过匹配载荷对（恶意文本相同，仅渠道变化），衡量模型对对抗性内容的敏感度如何随其到达用户消息、工具元数据或工具输出的不同而改变。在10个生产级LLM和三种攻击家族中，通用型模型对作为工具元数据到达的指令的敏感度远低于用户消息中的相同指令，而代理原生型模型的敏感度差异则小得多。这种差异在控制工具可用性和评分的匹配控制实验以及大小控制混合中依然存在。
tldr: 本文提出安全不对称分数（SAS），发现通用型语言模型对工具元数据中的恶意指令敏感度远低于用户消息，而代理原生型模型差异较小，揭示了信任渠道的不对称性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Safety Asymmetry Score (SAS), revealing that general-purpose language models are far less susceptible to malicious instructions in tool metadata than in user messages, while agent-native models show smaller differences, highlighting trust asymmetry across channels.
